why: The origins a browser puts on a request. Two things read them and both are a client-visible part of the answer: the CORS policy, which decides the headers, and the CSRF origin check, which decides whether a cookie-authenticated write happens at all. A foreign origin is also the only way to see a response whose CORS headers are written twice.

variants.label: no origin, as a server-to-server call has none
a null origin, as a sandboxed frame sends
an origin that is the site's with another port
a foreign origin with a matching referer
